headline: US stocks trade lower as escalating Middle East tensions lift oil prices and weigh on cyclicals and financials despite AI-linked tech strength
raw_text:
- Micron Technology (MU) rises after the Trump administration directs Apple to avoid Chinese DRAM suppliers, boosting demand for the leading U.S. memory producer
- Sandisk (SNDK) gains after the U.S. asks Apple to avoid Chinese memory competitors, potentially benefiting Sandisk (SNDK)’s iPhone-related memory business
- Western Digital (WDC) and Seagate (STX) trade higher alongside other storage hardware stocks benefiting from AI infrastructure demand
- Cerebras Systems (CBRS) jumps after a Wedbush note on OpenAI deal progression
- argenx advances sharply, extending recent momentum in biotech despite broader market weakness
- Vista Energy (VIST) climbs after Peter Thiel’s hedge fund discloses roughly a 1% stake in the company
- Major indices trade lower, with the S&P 500 (SPY), Dow (DIA), Nasdaq (QQQ) and Russell 2000 (IWM) pressured by rising geopolitical risk around the Strait of Hormuz and fresh Israel–Hezbollah violence
- The S&P 500 (SPY) tech sector trades modestly higher, partially offsetting selling in cyclicals, small caps and financials
- Goldman Sachs (GS) warns of a potential consumer spending slowdown, adding to pressure on domestically focused and cyclical names
- Empire State Manufacturing prints stronger than expected while the NAHB Housing Market Index draws a muted reaction as traders look ahead to upcoming retail earnings reports
